identification: Big Fish OpenBSD shared-memory/multicast local root exploit source
review: Independent second static review of the complete source, cleave facts and extracted x86-64 payload disassembly; no sample code executed and no external conviction relied upon.
evidence: do_wrap banks shmat records but munmaps their views, then forks enough processes to cross the signed 16-bit attachment-count boundary. Positive counts abort. IPC_RMID frees the segment while children retain stale records.

race_once waits for a transient attachment count, removes the segment, and reuses its slot with a 4 MiB segment. The helper attaches the dangling object; a four-page spray and a page-7 fault target adjacent multicast bookkeeping.

KERN_MALLOCSTATS guides poll/socket/readv heap grooming. readv(-1,...) primes freed M_IOV allocations; a second pipe readv holds controlled addresses in iov_base and iov_len beside the multicast membership vector. These sockets implement corruption, not C2 or exfiltration.

prepare_shell_page patches a 128-byte x86-64 payload and makes its mapped pages RX. Disassembly at payload offsets 0x10, 0x19 and 0x20 loads gs:[0x98], dereferences [rax+0x230], and writes zero to dword [rdx+8], consistent with the process credential UID field.

The forged multicast records aim two reference decrements at the recursive PTE and overwrite enc0 if_ioctl. close(target) triggers the walk. The payload restores the callback, repairs the membership loop and increments the UAO reference before returning.

After checking geteuid()==0, the program calls setresuid(0,0,0) and setresgid(0,0,0), forks and execls /bin/sh -p, optionally passing argv[1] to -c. This is a concrete attempt to cross the kernel privilege boundary.

No string obfuscation, network command channel, credential theft or victim-file destruction was established. The byte array is native executable code. Failure may leave corrupt kernel state, but the finite child bank is for reference-counter exploitation rather than a standalone fork bomb.
limitations: The source targets fixed OpenBSD 7.9 VM addresses/offsets. The exploit was not built or run; runtime success on a particular host is not asserted. Research provenance does not negate the privilege-escalation behavior.
changes: Preserved both hostile exploit composites and all original capabilities after ID mapping.
Added notable native mprotect call detection and connected it to the existing canonical mprotect composite. Comments, string constants and declarations are negative controls.

Relocated source socket creation, multicast configuration, interface lookup, shared mappings, mapped-page synchronization and function-pointer cast syntax. Matchers and effective scopes are unchanged.
Updated exact consumers and retained the moved source member in the legacy init selector. Ancestor mem consumers still contain all relocated memory operations.
Renamed the socket/poll composite to describe API co-occurrence. The sample uses poll with invalid descriptors for allocation retention; socket-plus-poll does not bind sockets to the poll set.
Changed the setsockopt import description to API reference, which accurately covers the source-call import projection.

Instruction-cache consumers now use the exact former cache-operation set through a named group, so mapped-file synchronization cannot satisfy a Windows injection claim. The hotpatch composite explicitly retains its formerly effective PE/DLL scope.
